crime_highlights: She was selling crack cocaine in the Main and Hastings area of Vancouver to support her own habit
she was found to be carrying 137 rocks of crack cocaine weighing 10.36 grams
rationale_highlights: although the sentence was lenient, it was appropriate in the circumstances of this offender
She is an aboriginal person and therefore entitled to the special consideration mandated by s. 718.2(e) of the Criminal Code
sentencing courts are to recognize the unique circumstances of aboriginal offenders and the fact of over-incarceration of aboriginal people in Canada
a restorative approach should be fully explored and incarceration considered a last resort
the range is difficult to ascertain here because the law has only recently evolved in the area of aboriginal offenders
judgment this sentence is not unfit
note: Appeal court relies on Gladue to uphold a lenient sentence; borderline but own view.

crime_highlights: the accused drove around at high speeds
the car went around a corner on the reserve, near the accused's home, and flipped on its aside
His reading was 230 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood
rationale_highlights: The learned sentencing judge here was a very experienced judge who was familiar with local conditions and the problems facing aboriginal communities
I am satisfied that he fully took into account the implications of that decision and the problems relating to sentencing of aboriginal offenders
note: Appeal court only says Gladue was considered; never says it reduced sentence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Rowell entered a Cold Beer and Wine Store during daylight hours and held a large kitchen knife along his arm and told the clerk that she was being robbed
The clerk was frightened but was not injured in this robbery
rationale_highlights: consider that there may be some impact from his aboriginal background, the fact that his family was split up and so on, which have contributed to his criminal record and past actions
perhaps because of some special problems that the people in aboriginal communities may have suffered as a result of loss of their society over a period of time and attempts to rebuild it
I can see no error in principle in the judge's reasons as to the Gladue case
Being mindful of this appellant's aboriginal background and the principles set out in Gladue I am unable to conclude that this sentence is other than a fit one
note: Background considered only; no court says it reduced culpability or sentence.
